text:
maya: Quick idea — add a "permissions diff" preview to the rollout UX so PMs and SREs can see what changes a role/entitlement rollout will actually grant across routes and quotas.

maya: Right now rollouts only show who toggled a flag and which role is assigned. We should show "effective permissions" by evaluating the policy graph and quota impacts :thinking:

sam: +1. Can we make it simulation-only (no write) and include a timeline of when the new perms take effect? e.g., canary -> 50% -> 100%

alex: We need telemetry hooks too. If we simulate 50% canary, output expected error rate increases for each route based on historical usage.

jin: POC idea: a CLI that calls /v1/internal/permissions/simulate with payload like:
```
POST /v1/internal/permissions/simulate
{
  "target_role": "ent_admin",
  "routes": ["/api/generate","/api/embeddings"],
  "traffic_split": {"canary":0.1, "prod":0.9}
}
```
Response would include diffs + estimated quota delta per tenant.

maya: Nice. UX wise I want an inline diff view: added/removed capabilities, quota delta, list of affected tenants with risk score. Low-risk suggestions should be collapsible.

sam: One caution — computing effective permissions requires evaluating scope inheritance + service accounts. Might be expensive for big orgs; we should cache per-role snapshots and invalidate on policy changes.

jin: Agreed. We can compute async and stream results. For large orgs show "estimating..." and show partial results as they arrive.

alex: Ops-bot FYI: existing rollout audit logs should link to simulation snapshots so reviewers can recreate the exact diff later :link:

ops-bot: Noted — added webhook for simulation snapshot storage to infra-archive queue. (automated)

maya: Ok next steps: sam/jin to draft API shape & perf plan, alex to mock UI, I'll sync with PMs on the risk scoring algorithm. I'll schedule 30m sync tomorrow 10:30am.

sam: I'll start with cache design. tagging this thread #rollouts #permissions

alex: will mock quick comps in Figma by EOD tomorrow.

maya: thanks all :raised_hands:
